title.source: Section check: War, independence and rebuilding
title.back: Section check: War, independence and rebuilding

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 7–9. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 7–9. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: What happened in Singapore on 15 February 1942?
questions.0.question.back: What happened in Singapore on 15 February 1942?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: The occupation came to an end.

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The occupation ended in 1945. On 15 February 1942, it began. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The occupation ended in 1945. 15 February 1942 is the day the occupation began. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. In 1942, Japanese lessons became compulsory in schools. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.note: "compulsory" (SAT07 glossary) is บังคับ, as in วิชาบังคับ. Second pass: checked against SAT07, it matches; flag removed.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. In 1942 Japanese became a compulsory subject in schools. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.0.options.2.text.back: The British army surrendered to Japan

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. British forces gave up at the Ford Factory. Then the occupation began. It lasted until 1945.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.note: Second pass: "surrendered" is now ยอมแพ้ in the option and the feedback, as in SAT07 (the option said ยอมจำนน); the Former Ford Factory is โรงงานฟอร์ดเก่า, as in SAT07 (questions.1.options.1 said อดีตโรงงานฟอร์ด). Flag removed.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. The British army surrendered at the Ford Factory. Then the Japanese occupation began and lasted until 1945.

questions.1.question.source: You want to learn what people in Singapore ate in 1943. Which source would help most?
questions.1.question.back: You want to know what people in Singapore ate in 1943. Which source would help most?

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Lee Geok Boi used oral history interviews to write about food in this time. Memories can tell us about meals.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Lee Geok Boi used oral history interviews to write about food in this time. Memories can tell us about food and eating.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: A 2025 photo of the Former Ford Factory
questions.1.options.1.text.back: A photo of the Former Ford Factory from 2025

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo shows the building in 2025. It cannot show what people ate in 1943. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. This picture shows the building in 2025. It cannot tell what people ate in 1943. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.1.options.2.text.back: The rule about learning Japanese in schools

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. That rule tells us about school lessons, not meals. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. That rule tells us about school learning, not food. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.2.question.source: On 17 August 1945, two leaders said in public that Indonesia was free. What is this kind of statement called?
questions.2.question.note: "said in public that Indonesia was free" avoids ประกาศ so the question does not give away the answer คำประกาศ. "statement" is ถ้อยแถลง. Indonesia's independence is a national day; keep the wording neutral and factual.
questions.2.question.back: On 17 August 1945, two leaders said in public that Indonesia was free. What is a statement like this called?

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A proclamation is a statement made to all. In Indonesia, people mark 17 August as the day they became free.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. A proclamation is a statement that lets everyone know. In Indonesia, people regard 17 August as the day the country became free.

questions.2.options.1.text.note: Second pass: "transfer of sovereignty" is now การส่งมอบอธิปไตย, the wording SAT08 uses throughout (was การโอนอธิปไตย). Flag removed.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The Netherlands handed over power later, in 1949. That came after the proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The Netherlands handed over power later, in 1949, which came after the proclamation. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A federation is a group of states joined under one main government. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A federation is a group of several states joined under one central government. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.3.question.source: A student says that Malaysia became free on 31 August 1957. What needs to change?
questions.3.question.back: A student says Malaysia became free on 31 August 1957. What needs correcting?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. 17 August 1945 is the date of Indonesia's proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. 17 August 1945 is the date of Indonesia's proclamation of independence. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: Change Malaysia to the Federation of Malaya
questions.3.options.1.text.note: "Federation of Malaya" is สหพันธรัฐมาลายา, the usual Thai name. Second pass: SAT08 uses the same name (with สหพันธ์ as the glossary word and สหพันธรัฐ as a form), so they already match; flag removed.
questions.3.options.1.text.back: Change Malaysia to the Federation of Malaya

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. It was the Federation of Malaya that became free in 1957. Malaysia was formed later, in 1963.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. What became free in 1957 was the Federation of Malaya. Malaysia was formed later, in 1963.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. In 1956, leaders signed an agreement in London. It set the day of independence in 1957. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. In 1956 leaders signed an agreement in London. This agreement set independence day in 1957. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.4.question.source: In March 2000, a UN report said many schools in Timor-Leste had been repaired. What does this date tell you?
questions.4.question.back: In March 2000, a United Nations report said many schools in Timor-Leste had been repaired. What does this date tell you?

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The report is from 2000. That is before independence was restored in 2002. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.note: Sensitive: "independence was restored in 2002" reflects Timor-Leste's view (independence first declared in 1975, then Indonesian rule). Second pass: now เอกราชของติมอร์-เลสเต...ฟื้นคืนมา, the wording and glossary word of SAT09, used across the course (was ได้เอกราชคืน). No judgement added. A native speaker should confirm it reads neutrally.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. This report is from 2000, before Timor-Leste's independence was restored in 2002. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Work on schools began before 2002, while a UN team ran the country with East Timorese leaders.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.note: "East Timorese leaders" is ผู้นำชาวติมอร์ตะวันออก; "a UN team ran the country" is ทีมของสหประชาชาติบริหารประเทศ. "transition" (SAT09 glossary) is ช่วงเปลี่ยนผ่าน.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. School repair work began before 2002, while the United Nations team ran the country with East Timorese leaders.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. 2024 is the date of the school photo. Repairs began much earlier. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. 2024 is the year the school photo was taken. Repairs began long before that. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.5.stimulus.title.source: A made-up school in a made-up town
questions.5.stimulus.title.back: A made-up school in a made-up town

questions.5.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. The made-up town of Lorvan has a new school building with a strong roof. But there are very few books. Most teachers have had no training. Many children do not understand the language used in class.
questions.5.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A made-up town called Lorvan has a new school building with a strong roof, but very few books. Most teachers have never been trained. Many children do not understand the language used in class.

questions.5.question.source: What would help the children in Lorvan learn the most?
questions.5.question.back: What would help the children in Lorvan learn most?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: New paint on the school walls

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The building is already fixed. A school needs more than walls. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The building is already fine. A school needs more than walls. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: A big party to open the school
questions.5.options.1.text.back: Hold a big event to open the school

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A party lasts one day. Learning needs teachers, books and a language children know. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A celebration lasts only one day. Learning needs teachers, books and a language children know. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Teachers, books and a known language
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Teachers, books and a language children know

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. In Timor-Leste, too, buildings were fixed first. Teachers, books and language are also needed for learning.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. It was the same in Timor-Leste: buildings were repaired first, but learning also needs teachers, books and language.

results.high.source: Well done. You kept the dates in order, and you saw what each source can show.
results.high.back: Great work. You put the dates in the right order and saw what each source can show.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Well done. You got many right. Go back to the lessons for the questions you have not got right yet, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 7–9, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 7–9 and try again. Take as long as you need.
